threads.subject: Ukraine 2022
threads.question:
From Lnomdn
Good day, I am writing to ask if the Ukrainian citizens entering Canada as part of the emergency travel visas are eligible to apply for IFHP under the following:
- Certain people who are being resettled in Canada as a result of a public policy or humanitarian and compassionate considerations on the Minister's own initiative
Yours truly,
threads.answer:
March 23. 2022 2:19 PM
Good day,
Thank you for submitting your inquiry to the Immigration Representatives Mailbox. We hope the following answers your question.
Q: I am writing to ask if the Ukrainian citizens entering Canada as part of the emergency travel visas are eligible to apply for IFHP under the following: Certain people who are being resettled in Canada as a result of a public policy or humanitarian and compassionate considerations on the Minister's own initiative
A: Foreign nationals affected by the situation in Ukraine, who are applying to come to Canada temporarily under the Canada-Ukraine Authorization for Emergency Travel (CUAET) program, are not eligible for Interim Federal Health
Program (IFHP) coverage.
Applicants and their family members may be eligible for insured health services through their province or territory with a valid open work permit or study permit, subject to certain conditions. Provinces and territories set eligibility for publicly-funded health-care in their jurisdictions and we would encourage all clients with health needs to reach out to their respective provincial or territorial health-insurance program, to explore programs for uninsured patients and/or apply for medical coverage.
Note that IFHP benefits are available for refugee claimants, in-Canada protected persons, and resettled refugees. For the purpose of the IFHP, resettled refugees includes government-assisted refugees, privately sponsored refugees, and certain groups of people who are being resettled as refugees in Canada as a result of a public policy, based on humanitarian and compassionate considerations, on the Minister's own initiative. Foreign nationals from Ukraine under the CUAET are not being resettled to Canada as refugees and therefore do qualify under the IFHP eligible groups.
For additional information on the IFHP's regular and discretionary programs, including eligibility, visit the IFHP's online policy statement.
Regards,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

*** Sections 2(i) and 3(h) are conditions (eligibility requirements) of the public policy applicable to the principal applicant in Canada which require that the foreign national:

To be eligible under the Temporary public policy to grant permanent residence to certain Ukrainian nationals with family in Canada-Canada.ca there are two key conditions regarding presence in Canada. threads.question:

Would it be possible to confirm whether individuals who hold a TRP and a WP that expire on the same day can continue working under implied status as long as renewals of both documents are requested (together) prior to expiry? threads.answer:
Mav 30, 2022 2:39 PM
RE: TRP/WP & Implied Status
Thank you for contacting the Immigration Representatives mailbox. We hope the following answers your question.
QUESTION:_Would it be possible to confirm whether individuals who hold a TRP and a WP that expire on the same day can continue working under implied status as long as renewals of both documents are requested (together) prior to expiry? What effect does the lack of maintained status in the context of a TRP renewal have on parallel work authorization?
RESPONSE:_Status and authorization are two separate things under the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations. There is no maintained status when applying for a subsequent Temporary Resident Permit (TRP). TRP's are issued under the authority of section 24 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and therefore do not meet the requirements of the status maintained by law under R183(5).
The authority to work is provided by Regulation (R186) or by issuance of a work permit. If a work permit holder submits an application to renew their work permit under R201 prior to the expiry of their existing work permit, then they may work under the authority of R186(u) with the same conditions (other than validity) of their existing work permit until a decision is made on the application. R186(u) does not require that the foreign national hold temporary resident status.

You have submitted two inquiries with similar questions. One in December 2016 below, and one in February 2017. reference number REP-2017-0283. It was responded to with the following information, which answers both inquiries:
What is the procedure, for a permanent resident of Canada who won their appeal at IAD on Residency Obligation (for a PR applied for PRTD and was found by the Visa office not to have met the Residency obligation, but the decision of officer was set aside by the lAD).
Will the Visa office continue to process the PRTD? In a situation where the Immigration Appeal Division (lAD) of the Immigration and Refugee Board (IRB) allows an appeal of a negative residency determination decision made outside of Canada, the lAD sets aside the original decision and as per subsection 67(2) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and will "substitute a determination that, in its opinion, should have been made, including the making of a removal order, or refer the matter to the appropriate decision-maker for reconsideration." Where an appeal of a negative residency determination is allowed, the CBSA will inform IRCC of the IAD decision so that IRCC may take the necessary steps which will depend on the specific decision made by the lAD. The client would not need to make a new PRTD application as the original application would continue to be processed. The client may, however, wish to provide the notice they received from the lAD that the appeal was allowed to the processing office. There is no specific timeframe for the office to complete the processing of the PRTD application following the lAD's decision; however, as soon as IRCC receives notification of the lAD decision, they will process the request as quickly as possible. Should the client wish to do so, they may also provide the notice they received from the lAD that the appeal was allowed to the processing office. If the application is taking longer than expected or the client needs to contact IRCC for any other reason regarding their PRTD application, they may contact the office processing their application. Sent: Fri. 12 Mav 2017 14:58:16
Bonjour,
Je vous remercie pour votre enquête concernant les cours en ligne.
Le Ministère définit l'apprentissage à distance comme un processus dans le cadre duquel la technologie est utilisée de manière à ce que l'étudiant n'ait pas besoin d'être physiquement présent à l'endroit où se donne l'enseignement. L'apprentissage à distance est offert sous diverses formes : en ligne, par correspondance ou par Internet.
Dans le cas d’une demande de renouvellement de permis d’études et d’un étranger qui peut présenter une demande de permis d’études au Canada, l’agent doit délivrer un permis d’études (et un permis de travail, s’il y a lieu) lorsqu’il est convaincu que le demandeur répond à tous les critères de recevabilité et d’admissibilité. Selon Section 220.1 (1) de la loi sur l’immigration et la protection des réfugiés et règlements (IPRR), le titulaire d'un permis d'études au Canada est assujetti aux conditions suivantes :
a) il est inscrit dans un établissement d’enseignement désigné et demeure inscrit dans un tel établissement jusqu'à ce qu'il termine ses études;
b) il suit activement un cours ou son programme d’études.
Pour obtenir un permis de travail au titre du programme de permis de travail postdiplôme (PPTPD), le demandeur doit répondre aux critères suivants :
avoir un permis d’études valide lorsqu'il présente une demande de permis de travail; avoir été, sans interruption, un étudiant à plein temps au Canada (c.-à-d. dans un établissement d'enseignement canadien) et avoir terminé un programme d’études d’une durée minimale de huit mois; avoir terminé avec succès le programme d’études et reçu de l’établissement d’enseignement un document l’avisant qu’il est admissible à l'obtention de son diplôme ou de son certificat. Il doit être diplômé de l'un des types d'établissements suivants : un établissement d’enseignement postsecondaire public, tel qu’un collège, une école technique ou de métiers, une université ou un collège d'enseignement général et professionnel (cégep) au Québec, un établissement d'enseignement postsecondaire privé assujetti aux mêmes règlements que les établissements postsecondaires publics, un établissement d’enseignement secondaire ou postsecondaire privé (au Québec) offrant des programmes admissibles d’une durée de 900 heures ou plus menant à l’obtention d'un diplôme d’études professionnelles (DEP) ou d’une attestation de spécialisation professionnelle (ASP), un établissement d’enseignement canadien privé autorisé à décerner des diplômes (c.-à-d. un baccalauréat, une maîtrise ou un doctorat) en vertu d’une loi provinciale, mais seulement si l'étudiant est inscrit à un programme d’études reconnu par la province menant à l’obtention d’un diplôme, et non à n’importe quel programme d'études offert par l’établissement d’enseignement privé. Le demandeur doit présenter une demande de permis de travail dans les 90 jours qui suivent la réception d’un document (p. ex. une lettre ou un relevé de notes officiels) de l’établissement d’enseignement précisant qu'il a satisfait aux exigences liées à l’achèvement de son programme d'études. Le décompte des 90 jours commence le jour où les notes finales de l'étudiant sont communiquées ou à la réception d'un avis officiel écrit de l’établissement d'enseignement signifiant la réussite du programme par l’étudiant, selon la première éventualité.
Autres facteurs à prendre en considération : L'étudiant qui termine un programme d'apprentissage à distance (au Canada ou à l’étranger) n'est pas admissible au
PPTPD. Les agents peuvent appliquer les lignes directrices suivantes pour évaluer l'admissibilité d’un demandeur au PPTPD lorsque celui-ci a suivi, dans un EED, des cours à distance ou en ligne au Canada :
si moins de la majorité de l’ensemble des crédits obtenus par l’étudiant en vue de terminer un programme d’études ont été obtenus dans le cadre d’un apprentissage en ligne, un permis de travail postdiplôme peut être délivré en fonction de la durée du programme précisée par l'EED, y compris les crédits obtenus dans le cadre de cours offerts en classe et en ligne; si la majorité des crédits obtenus par l’étudiant en wue de terminer un programme d’études ont été obtenus dans le cadre d’un apprentissage en ligne, le demandeur n’est pas admissible au PPTPD étant donné que le programme peut être raisonnablement considéré comme un programme d’apprentissage à distance. Voir : [http://www.cic.gc.ca/francais/ressources/outils/temp/etudiants/post-diplome.asp](http://www.cic.gc.ca/francais/ressources/outils/temp/etudiants/post-diplome.asp) et [http://www.cic.gc.ca/francais/ressources/outils/temp/etudiants/contrainte.asp](http://www.cic.gc.ca/francais/ressources/outils/temp/etudiants/contrainte.asp)
Cordialement,
La boîte aux lettres des représentants en immigration

threads.answer:
Sent: Tue. 23 Mav 2017 15:22:33
Dear M
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives mailbox.
In response to your enquiry:
Case A
Can an applicant for Express Entry use an expired IELTS result to create his profile?
Response: No. Any language test results that are expired (two years old or more) will result in an applicant being ineligible at profile submission. If a candidate submits a language test result that is valid when they submit their profile and is placed into the pool, they will become ineligible and be removed from the pool on the date that their language test results expire.
The applicant did created one profile and received an ITA and a new test has been booked. The applicant is expecting an equal or higher score. If that happens, will the applicant have success in accepting the invitation and submitting the new results?
Response: Yes. If a candidate is invited to apply and the language test expires after the date they were invited and before the date they submit their application for permanent residence, they may submit a new language test result with their application.
Case B
Applicant has a job offer for two years. The work permit was approved based on a positive LMIA and the applicant is working for the employer since January 2017. Can the applicant request additional points for arranged employment for Express Entry-FSW based on those conditions? If we consider applying now, the applicant may receive an ITA very soon. Considering the processing time of 6 months, the applicant still under conditions of that job offer for the next year.
Response: Per section 29 of the Ministerial Instructions, if a foreign national has a qualifying offer of arranged employment, they may be assigned points as follows:
- (a) 200 points, if the offer is for employment in an occupation contained in Major Group 00 of the National Occupation Classification; or
(b) 50 points, if the offer is any other qualifying offer of arranged employment.
Qualifying offer of arranged employment
(2) A qualifying offer of employment is one of the following:
- (a) an arranged employment as defined in subsection 82(1) of the Regulations, if
(i) the offer is supported by a valid assessment — provided by the Department of Employment and Social Development at the request of the employer or an officer and on the same basis as an assessment provided for the issuance of a work permit — that the requirements set out in subsection 203(1) of the Regulations with respect to the offer have been met, (ii) the foreign national holds a valid work permit, the offer of employment is made by an employer for whom the foreign national currently works and who is specified on the work permit, the work permit was issued based on a positive determination made by an officer under subsection 203(1) of the Regulations with respect to the foreign national's employment with that employer in an occupation that is listed in Skill Type 0 Management Occupations or Skill Level A or B of the National Occupational Classification matrix and the assessment provided by the Department of Employment
and Social Development on the basis of which the determination was made is not suspended or revoked, or (iii) the foreign national holds a valid work permit issued under the circumstances described in paragraph 204(a) or (c) or section 205 of the Regulations, the offer is made by an employer who is specified on the work permit and the foreign national works for that employer and has accumulated at least one year of full-time work experience, or the equivalent in part-time work, over a continuous period of work for that employer;
(b) an offer of continuous full-time employment for a total duration of at least one year from the day on which a permanent resident visa is issued in a skilled trade occupation as defined in subsection 87.2(1) of the Regulations that is made to the foreign national by up to two employers, neither of which is an embassy, high commission or consulate in Canada or an employer referred to in any of subparagraphs 200(3)(h)(i) to (iii) of the Regulations if
(i) the offer is supported by a valid assessment — provided by the Department of Employment and Social Development at the request of one or two employers or an officer and on the same basis as an assessment provided for the issuance of a work permit — that the requirements set out in subsection 203(1) of the Regulations with respect to the offer have been met, (ii) the foreign national holds a valid work permit, the offer is made by up to two employers who are specified on the work permit, the foreign national currently works for one of those employers, the work permit was issued on the basis of a positive determination by an officer under subsection 203(1) of the Regulations with respect to their employment with their current employer, the assessment by the Department of Employment and Social Development on which the determination is based is not revoked or suspended, and the offer is in a skilled trade occupation that is in the same minor group set out in the National Occupational Classification as the occupation specified on the work permit, or (iii) the foreign national holds a valid work permit issued under the circumstances described in paragraph 204(a) or (c) or section 205 of the Regulations that specifies the employer or employers that made the offer, and the foreign national works for an employer specified on the permit and has accumulated a total of at least one year of full-time work experience, or the equivalent in part-time work, over a continuous period of work for the employers who made the offer.
In order for your client to be assigned points for having a qualified offer of arranged employment, you must demonstrate by answering questions in the Express Entry system that the above-mentioned criteria are met.
We trust this information will assist you.

Good Day,
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives mailbox. We appreciate your patience.
Here is the response for Question 1.
1. To be eligible for C11 work permit as an entrepreneur, you either need to:
a. Have a nomination certificate from a province such as the Ontario Provincial Nominee Program for Entrepreneurs (dual intent) – OR
b. Have a temporary intent
1a. False. You do not need to have a nomination certificate but if the foreign national intends to eventually seek a nomination, the work permit application must be accompanied by a letter of support from the province.
1b. False, the foreign national can have dual intent, however, their status is as a temporary resident. As stated in the
program delivery instructions for LMIA-exemption code C11 – Entrepreneurs/self-employed candidates seeking to operate
a business:
As per subsection 22(2) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, applicants who have a dual intent to seek status as temporary workers and then eventually as permanent residents must satisfy the officer that they have the ability and willingness to leave Canada at the end of the temporary period authorized under section 183 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations.
Question 2. If you are a self-employed applicant seeking only temporary residence (b.temporary intent), you will NOT get any points from your C11 work permit under the Federal Skilled Worker program if you already meet the work experience requirement (at least 1 year of full-time continuous work experience under NOC 0, A or B). This means that you will NOT get any points for your past work in Canada neither any point for arranged employment.
Answer 2: we would like to highlight that self-employment work experience may qualify under Federal Skilled Workers program, however, it does not count towards the Minimum Eligibility Criteria (MEC) of the Canadian Experience Class (CEC) nor does it count to obtain the CRS points for Canadian Work Experience in Express Entry.
Section 15(7)(b) of the Ministerial Instructions respecting the Express Entry system states:
(7) For the purposes of this section, •(a) a period of employment during which the foreign national was engaged in full-time study is not to be included in calculating a period of work experience;
mmigration, Refugees nmigration, Réfugiés Citoyenneté Canada
- (b) a period of self-employment or unauthorized work is not to be included in calculating a period of work experience;
- (c) the foreign national must have had temporary resident status during their period of work experience and any period of full-time study or training; and
- (d) the full-time equivalent for part-time work experience is 30 hours of work per week.
Self-employed applicants may still be eligible for an Express Entry program and they may be able to obtain points for qualifying offer of arranged employment if they meet the criteria as per section 29(2)(a)(ii) and (iii) of the Ministerial Instructions respecting the Express Entry system. Self-employment would not fall under either section 29(2)(a)(ii) and (iii)of the Ministerial Instructions.
Section 29 (2) states: A qualifying offer of employment is one of the following:
(a) an arranged employment as defined in subsection 82(1) of the Regulations, if
(i) the offer is supported by a valid assessment — provided by the Department of Employment and Social Development at the request of the employer or an officer and on the same basis as an assessment provided for the issuance of a work permit — that the requirements set out in subsection 203(1) of the Regulations with respect to the offer have been met, o(ii) the foreign national holds a valid work permit, the offer of employment is made by an employer for whom the foreign national currently works and who is specified on the work permit, the work permit was issued based on a positive determination made by an officer under subsection 203(1) of the Regulations with respect to the foreign national's employment with that employer in an occupation that is listed in Skil Type 0 Management Occupations or Skill Level A or B of the National Occupational Classification matrix and the assessment provided by the Department of Employment and Social Development on the basis of which the determination was made is not suspended or revoked, or o (iii) the foreign national holds a valid work permit issued under the circumstances described in paragraph 204(a) or (c) or section 205 of the Regulations, the offer is made by an employer who is specified on the work permit and the foreign national works for that employer and has accumulated at least one year of full-time work experience, or the equivalent in part-time work, over a continuous period of work in Canada for that employer;
The assessment of an application is based on a case-by-case basis, each application will be considered on its own merits, with a final decision based on a review of all the information available to the officer at the time of decision. The onus is always on the applicant to provide sufficient documentation to satisfy an officer that they meet the requirements.

threads.question: We understand that a Study Permit automatically becomes invalid after 90 days of completion of study program even if the Expiry date on the Study Permit has another 1 month to expiry the expiry date. For such a situation if it is already past 90 days since graduation of study program, but study permit expiry date stated on the existing Study Permit still has another 1 month to the expiry date, can an application of a C50 Work Permit be done at the same time with restoration of status? Payment of restoration fee of $350 (restoration plus study permit fees) and $155 (C50 Wo0rk Permit application fee) all paid at the same time as the application of the C50 Work Permit?
threads.answer:
The Restoration of status program delivery instructions provide :
[Ninety-day period
Foreign nationals have 90 days from the date they lose their temporary resident status to apply for restoration. Under section A47, status is lost on expiry of the period of authorized stay or on determination by an officer that
the foreign national has failed to comply with any other requirement of the IRPA.
under section A47,
a period of authorized stay includes periods of status imposed by law (implied status) under
subsection R183(5) if an application is rejected under section R12 as incomplete, there is no extension of the period
of authorized stay (implied status)
under paragraph R222(1)(a), a study permit becomes invalid 90 days after the student completes their
program of study]
The period of authorized stay ends when the permit becomes invalid.
The IRPR stipulate:
R183(4)(b) The period authorized for a temporary resident's stay ends on the earliest of the day on which their permit becomes invalid, in the case of a temporary resident who has been issued either a work permit or a study permit;
R222(1)(a) A study permit becomes invalid upon the first to occur of the following days the day that is 90 days after the day on which the permit holder completes their studies
Since the foreign national's study permit became invalid 90 days after they completed their program of study, the restoration period begins the day after their study permit becomes invalid.
Citoyenneté Canada
Considering the above references, if a person is issued a study permit valid from January 1, 2021 to June 30, 2023 and they finish their studies on December 31, 2022. Their SP becomes invalid on March 31, 2023 not on June 30, 2023.
As such they would have 90 days from March 31, 2023 to apply for restoration of status.
Please follow the instruction found under: Example: You want to apply for a different work permit, but your study permit has expired found on this page: Restore your status and get a work permit. You may submit the study permit application with restoration request without a letter of acceptance as long as the work permit application is in the same package.
Clients should be submitting the IMM 5710, pay the fees for that within the application and submit a separate receipt for $350 for the study permit and restoration request. We would suggest including a statement indicating what they are doing.

Good Day,
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives mailbox. We appreciate your patience.
Question: What is the exact definition of ‘qualifying offer of arranged employment'?
Answer: The Ministerial Instructions respecting the Express Entry system defines the term qualifying offer of arranged employment under section 29. If the applicant meets the criteria listed under section 29(1) or 29(2), they would be assigned either 200 or 50 CRS points. These would be points assigned under the Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS). Requirements differ between Express Entry programs regarding arranged employment and job offers. Our website defines what's required for each program, and includes various employment scenarios. The job offer presented in the application would be reviewed for program eligibility.
Question: What is the definition of ‘apply to IRCC for permanent residency' in the ESDC document?
Answer: Questions regarding ESDC owned documents must be referred to ESDC. For Express Entry, you can only apply for permanent residence if you receive an invitation to apply (ITA). Applicants must then respond to the ITA by submitting a complete application within 60 days, or declining the ITA. More information on the application process can be found on our website.
Question: How do you define floating an express entry profile? As the E.E only caters to the permanent residency stream, does EOl comes under the expression ‘applying for permanent residency' as without EOl there cannot be any ITA? Or is an invitation to apply (ITA) 'only' means applying. If it is true, then the expression in ESDC LMIA document that a person must apply for permanent residency before a validity period contradicts the process of applying under E.E. Technically, if EOl does not come under the definition of applying for permanent residency, the person can never apply but can only be ‘invited' to apply. This makes the validity of a document meaningless as a person in their capacity cannot technically apply but can only be invited to apply. So, simply, does EOl come under the expression of applying for permanent residency or not?
Answer: Your assumption is correct. Expression of Interest is not considered under the definition of “applying for permanent residence." For Express Entry, you can only apply for permanent residence if you receive an invitation to apply (ITA). Information regarding the most recent rounds of invitation can be found on our website.
Question: Under section 29 (2)(a), the qualifying offer of employment is the arrange employment as defined under R82(1) 'if supported by a valid assessment provided by ESDC'. How is the term 'valid' defined? In simple terms, for instance, a qualifying offer of employment is given to applicant ABC for 2 years. It does not talk about the validity of LMIA at the point of ITA.
Answer: The validity period refers to the LMIA validity period on the LMIA provided by ESDC. The applicant must have applied for the work permit, or permanent residence prior to the LMIA validity period. A valid assessment, under the context of section 29(2)(a)(i) of the Ministerial Instructions respecting the Express Entry system means that the arranged employment points would only be given if the LMIA was valid at the time of the permanent residency application. threads.answer:

RE: Study Permit Requirement-post-secondary institutions
Thank you for contacting the Immigration Representatives mailbox. We hope the following answers your question.
Learning institutions in Canada play an active role in the promotion, recruitment and admission of international students. DLls are a key source of information on the enrolment status of international students. DLls support the objectives of IRCC's regulatory changes by completing and submitting compliance verification requests through the DLI
Portal.
DLls may ensure that their students hold a valid study permit, as it is outlined in the student's study permit conditions unless the individual is enrolled in short time studies (a program that is 6 months or less).
As per the agreement between each province/territory (PT) and IRCC, DLIs may be asked to complete two types of compliance verification requests (Periodic verifications done twice a year in the spring and fall, and Ad hoc verifications). DLls complete these requests by submitting compliance verification reports through the DLl portal. Information collected through the DLl portal will allow us to assess whether study permit holders in Canada continue to meet their study permit conditions, including whether they are actively pursuing their course or program of study at a
DLI.
IRCC suggests appointing a primary and secondary representative to ensure that they start the report early so that IRCC can assist them in case the DLl has questions about their report. Furthermore, appointing both a primary and secondary user ensures that the DLl receives and submits their report on time to avoid the loss of designation. The primary contact at each post-secondary DLl will receive an email notification from us when a report becomes available for completion and submission.
DLIs have 60 days to complete the compliance report and 10 business days to respond to Ad Hoc verification requests. Failure to report within the required timeframe could result in loss of designation if the PT representative decides the school did not meet the requirements to remain a DLl. Each province and territory has its own criteria for accrediting schools, so you should get in touch with your PT representative.
For further information on the roles and responsibilities of DLls, please see the link below: [https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/partners-service-providers/dli-portal/compliance-reporting-guide.html](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/partners-service-providers/dli-portal/compliance-reporting-guide.html)
We hope that this information is helpful to you.
and Citizenshi Canada et Ciloyeneé Canada
Regards,

RP en cours -- REP-2022-0049
Bonjour,
La présente est en réponse à votre correspondance en date du 11 janvier 2022
Conformément à la politique générale du Ministère, IRCC exige que tout changement dans la composition de la famille soit noté avant l’acquisition de la résidence permanente.
Dans le contexte d'une demande CH, les demandeurs doivent déclarer un/une conjoint(e) (ou un autre membre de la famille) avant qu'une décision finale soit prise. Le lien de parenté avec le demandeur principal sera évalué et le membre de la famille devra faire l'objet d'un examen pour déterminer s'il est interdit de territoire afin que le Ministère peut procéder à l'octroi du statut de résident permanent.
Comme il est indiqué dans votre demande, la conjointe du demandeur fait l'objet d'une mesure de renvoi conditionnelle en tant que demandeur d'asile, ce qui le rend interdit de territoire, et conformément au paragraphe 25(1) de la Loi sur l'immigration et la protection des réfugiés, les étrangers qui ont présentés une demande d'asile peuvent être sujette à une interdiction de demander des considérations humanitaires.
Si la conjointe fait l'objet d'une interdiction de présenter une demande CH, elle peut être identifiée comme n'accompagnant pas le demandeur. Le demandeur d'asile n'est pas considéré comme un demandeur de résidence permanente ou un demandeur CH et aucun frais n'est à payer. Une demande visant à contourner la disposition relative aux membres de la famille interdits de territoire pourrait être présentée pour le demandeur, et ce dernier pourrait demander à parrainer sa conjointe lorsqu'il deviendra un résident permanent.
Nous vous remercions et nous espérons que ces informations vous seront utiles,
La boîte aux lettres des représentants de l'immigration

Hello!
The recently announced IRCC regulations indicate that international students with valid study permits may need to apply for a new study permit when changing their designated learning institution (DLl) in most situations. However, there are scenarios (below) that do not clearly align with the examples provided on the IRCC guidelines page. [https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/change-schools.html](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/change-schools.html)
1. Scenario 1: Prerequisite Courses at a Secondary Institution A student is currently enrolled in a degree program at a university (DLI) but requires prerequisite high school courses. These courses would be attended simultaneously at a secondary school while the student remains enrolled in their degree program at the university. Since the student is not changing their primary institution but is attending a single course at a secondary school, would they still be required to apply for a new study permit to take this course?
A: Secondary students whose permit only authorizes studies at the primary or secondary level must apply for a new study permit in order to pursue studies at the post-secondary level. This also applies to post-secondary study permit holders, whose permit names a DLl or limits their studies to the post-secondary level, who wish to attend a secondary school program/course, even though the student is not changing their primary institution. Therefore, individuals transitioning between post-secondary and secondary level need to get a new study permit by applying to extend their current one to attend a secondary school.
2. Scenario 2: Cross-Institutional Enrollment for a Single Course Some students encounter situations where a required course is unavailable at their current university (DLl). In such cases, they obtain a letter of permission from their primary institution to take the course at another DLi (university) for one term, with the intention of transferring the credit back to their primary DLl (the one listed on their study permit). In this scenario, since the student is not permanently changing their DLI but is only attending a single course at another institution temporarily, would they need to apply for a new study permit?
A: Since November 08, 2024, post-secondary study permit holders must be enrolled at the designated learning institution (DLI) named on their permit. If a study permit holder wishes to concurrently attend more than one DLI, they must apply for a study permit for each DLl at which they intend to study.
As these scenarios are not explicitly addressed in the current guidelines, clarification on these matters would greatly help us provide accurate advice to international students.
Thank you for your guidance.
Regards,
Citoyenneté Canada

Question 1: Does R222(1)(a.1) apply to students whose study permit does not name a designated learning institution on it?
Answer 1: If a student is no longer enrolled at the designated learning institution (DLl) named in their study permit and does not have the DLI's name on their study permit, then subparagraph IRPR 222(1)(a.1) would not be applicable to them.
Question 2: Does the 90-day window to restore status apply to students who lose their status under R222(1)(a.1)? For example, if a student withdraws and would like to wait to leave Canada while a refund of tuition for the future terms is processed (less than 90 days), must they take action to maintain their status in Canada (i.e. apply for visitor status before they withdraw), or, given the 90-day restoration period, can they remain in Canada without taking action for a maximum of 90 days?
Answer 2:
A study permit holder must meet their study permit conditions. In such cases where the student is withdrawn due to not meeting previous study permit conditions, the student is considered "no longer enrolled". If you do not abide to the conditions of your study permit you may need to change your status, or leave Canada. However, there are a few cases where a student may be able to take a leave of up to a maximum of 150 days from their program of studies and still be actively pursuing their studies.
For more information, please refer to the IRCC website
Question 3: If a student withdraws from their DLl, but applies and is accepted to a different program at the same DLI starting 150 days or less after withdrawing from the initial program, and the study permit's expiry date has not passed, can they continue studying with the same study permit, or, given R111(1)(a.1), must they apply for a new study permit?
Answer 3: Students may, in exceptional circumstances, take a leave from their studies. The student must resume classes within 150 days of the date on which they stopped studying. There are various examples of reasons listed on the IRCC website Study Permits: Assessing study permit conditions-Canada.ca such as a change in program of study within the same institution. As of November 8, 2024, IRCC compliance reports are mandatory where the DLI must select the appropriate student's academic status at the DLI. IRCC's website provides several enrollment status options such as leave of absence, deferred enrollment, academic suspension, no longer registered etc. We ask you that you carefully review each definition.
Academic suspension The student is suspended from your institution, due to poor academic performance or violation of the institution's policies. The student is allowed to return after the period of suspension.
Any leave from a program of studies in Canada should not exceed 150 consecutive days from the date the leave started. If a student exceeds 150 days of leave from studies, they will need to change their status with IRCC or will be considered non- compliant with their study permit conditions.
No longer registered or enrolled Your institution sent the student a letter of admission, but they are no longer registered or enrolled because they have
- * been dismissed
* withdrawn voluntarily
- * transferred to another institution
Therefore, there is a difference between a student returning after a suspension and one no longer registered due to a withdrawal. If a student withdraws and is no longer enrolled at a DLl, they are no longer meeting the conditions of their study permit.
Question 4: If a student withdraws from their DLl, but applies and is accepted to resume the same program at the same DLl starting 150 days or less after withdrawing from the initial program, and the study permit's expiry date has not passed, can they continue studying with the same study permit, or, given R111(1)(a.1), must they apply for a new study permit?
Answer 4: See above

The foreign national may be eligible for a transfer in a specialized knowledge position in the Canadian enterprise since, at the time they submit the work permit extension application for their new role, they have 1 year of experience as a specialized knowledge worker within the last 3 years. In addition to this requirement, the foreign national would need to demonstrate that they hold a specialized knowledge position with the foreign enterprise.
If the Canadian enterprise promoted the foreign national to manager, but the foreign enterprise continues to hold available a position in a specialized knowledge capacity for the foreign national, they would not meet the at-level employment requirement.

Answer:
Please refer to the Ministerial Instructions respecting the Express Entry system to learn more about foreign work experience.
In order for work that is performed while physically outside of Canada to be considered foreign work experience, it must meet all the requirements. Foreign work experience is defined as work experience that
- * is acquired by a foreign national outside Canada in one or more occupations listed in TEER Category 0, 1, 2 or 3 of the National Occupational Classification;
* consists of full-time work experience, or equivalent part-time experience, with one or more employers;
* is acquired within the 10-year period preceding the application
- * is paid by wages or a commission.
It is possible to obtain foreign work experience by working remotely from abroad for a Canadian employer. Please be advised that the assessment of an application is conducted on a case-by-case basis, taking into consideration the specific circumstances and the supporting documentation available to the officer. When it comes to duration of employment as per LMIA, officers may issue a work permit for lesser duration than the LMIA for
Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR) Section 52 requires a foreign national to hold a passport that is valid for the entire length of their stay. Processing officers issue a work permit for the duration of work indicated in the LMIA provided that the passport is valid for the entire period. Where the passport expires before the specified duration of work, the work permit must be issued for a shorter duration than identified in the LMIA. For example, if the LMiA work duration is 2 years but the foreign national's passport will expire in 1 year, the officer will issue a 1-year work permit.
When issuing a work permit based on an approved LMIA for foreign nationals who are working under paragraph R186(u) and applying to continue working with the same employer, the officer calculates the extension period from the expiry date of the previous work permit and not from the date of approval. This ensures that the duration of work as stated in the LMIA is respected. For example, if the employment duration in the LMIA is 12 months and the foreign worker had been on maintained status with authority to work without a permit for 3 months before a decision was made on the work permit application, the officer would issue a work permit that is valid for 9 months from the date of the decision.
For more information on Duration of employment as per the LMIA, please consult: [https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-) refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-manuals/temporary-residents/foreign-

- * Reconsiderations are typically done in cases of application refusal and are submitted via regular channels like the IRCC Webform. Reconsideration should only be done, where warranted, in exceptional cases. An applicant's dissatisfaction or disagreement with the decision does not by itself qualify as an exceptional case. The onus is on the applicant to satisfy the officer that reconsideration is warranted. They may do so by submitting additional evidence to satisfy any officer concerns.

- * As noted above, the expiry date on the work permit is set based on: o * The date the LMiA/job offer is set to expire (keeping in mind maintained status); or o* The expiry date of the passport
- * If you are absolutely certain an error has been made by an immigration official concerning the duration of the work permit issued, the above mentioned reconsideration request or amendment application would be a first step as opposed to a new application entirely.
- * Normally, an LMiA cannot be re-used; however, if the work permit duration was shortened due to the passport validity, you can do so. As long as the LMIA's duration of work is still valid, you can submit a new work permit application with new fees and your updated passport. It is suggested that you include a letter to indicate the situation and that you are reusing an existing LMIA. This is simply to make sure that the processing officer does not miss the LMIA requirement given it's been associated to an existing application that has already been finalized.

Professional training programs A professional training program is a type of additional education or training usually offered to professionals already in the field. *** Q1: During Express Entry profile creation, we are entering all full-time and part-time work experience (even Teer 4-5), even during full-time studies. Correct? Answer: Yes, this is correct. All full-time and part-time work experience, even while studying full-time should be entered. The system will calculate the comprehensive ranking system (CRS) points based on this information.
Q2: PGWP holders often ask if they could study Master's Degree with a new Study Permit:

Answer: As per paragraph R87.1(3)(a) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations, any period of employment during which the foreign national was engaged in full-time study shall not be included in calculating a period of work experience under the Canadian Experience Class. **Background**
IRCC's public guidance (webpage: "Work in Canada after you graduate: Post-graduation work permit") states that PGWP holders "may take any course they like, including those longer than six months; however, they must apply for a study permit if the program is longer than six months."
However, IRPR 188(1)(c) permits foreign nationals to study without a study permit only if the course "is completed within the period for their stay initially authorized." For international graduates, the "period originally authorized" was typically tied to their previous study permit, which expired upon the issuance of the PGWP. This wording suggests that the exemption applies only to the time between initial entry and study permit expiry, and not to the subsequent PGWP period.
This discrepancy has led to uncertainty among practitioners and PGWP holders. While many rely on the clear language of the IRCC web guidance, a literal interpretation of IRPR 188(1)(c) implies that PGWP holders could be non-compliant if they engage in any study after their study permit expires—even for programs six months or shorter—unless they obtain a new study permit.

Questions
- * Partant du fait qu'il n’est pas inscrit dans l’établissement B et que rien ne lui est reconnu par cet établissement, a-t-il besoin d’une autre autorisation que son permis d’études existant?
■* Réponse : Aucun autre permis d’études ne sera nécessaire puisque l’étudiant n’est pas inscrit à l’établissement B et n’y est pas reconnu.
- * Est-il juste de dire que, autant lorsqu’il va sur le terrain que lorsqu’il fait des essais dans l’établissement B, l’étudiant
Ln est autorisé à mener ses essais grâce à son permis d’études, car ce sont des activités directement liées à sa formation doctorale créditée dans l’établissement A? o * Si non, quelle autorisation devrait-il obtenir pour mener les activités décrites qui sont partie intégrante de son doctorat? ■* Réponse : Selon les informations fournies, les activités décrites pourraient exiger un permis de travail COOP. L’établissement devra fournir une lettre à l’étudiant qui explique l’exigence de faire des activités de recherches soit en entreprise, sur le terrain ou dans tout autre établissement dans le cadre son
programme de doctorat et d’y décrire les spécificités.
Commentaire : Que ce soit pour aller faire des expériences sur le terrain ou dans l'établissement B en lien avec son doctorat, il ne s'agit pas d'activités jugées professionnelles. Je ne vois pas en vertu de quelle définition on pourrait considérer que c'est du travail puisqu'il ne s'agit ni d'une activité pour laquelle quelqu'un serait habituellement payé ni d'une activité qui représente une expérience de travail.
Méme si on convenait qu'il s'agit de travail, puisque ces activités ne sont pas obligatoires dans les programmes d’études et qu'elles sont planifiées à la pièce selon le projet de l'étudiant, cela ne répond pas aux critères d'admissibilité du permis de travail COOP et il est impossible pour l'établissement de faire une lettre précisant que c'est une exigence du programme.
Et quelles seraient les programmes qui lui permettrait de les obtenir? ■* Réponse : Un permis de travail COOP est nécessaire pour tout programme qui nécessite un stage ou une activité jugée professionnelle. o * Si oui, existe-t-il de règles publiées à cet effet ou une jurisprudence sur le sujet? ■*Réponse : De plus amples informations sont disponibles sur le site internet d'IRCC. o * Si oui, et considérant que son doctorat est d’une durée prévue de 4 ans, combien de temps l’étudiant pourrait-
il mener des essais dans l’établissement B sans contrevenir aux conditions de son permis d’études?
■* Réponse : Dans le cadre d’un stage coop, ou professionnel, l’activité ne doit pas excéder 50% de la durée du programme.
Questions dérivées
- * Si le codirecteur de l’étudiant n’était pas associé à l’établissement A, le raisonnement resterait-il le même?
* Réponse: Oui.
- * Si l’étudiant recevait une bourse d’études dans l’établissement B, durant les mois où il s’y trouve, cela changerait-il la donne? 0 * Réponse : Non.
- * Si l’établissement B était une entreprise plutôt qu’une université, mais que l’étudiant y menait aussi une activité de recherche créditée dans l’établissement A et décrite dans son programme de doctorat, la même logique s’appliquerait-elle? Est-ce que le fait qu’il y ait une bourse ou une rémunération de la part de l’entreprise changerait quelque chose? o * Réponse : Le fait d’obtenir une bourse ou non n’est pas un facteur mais plutôt le fait qu’une activité de recherche (et spécifier les tâches) est nécessaire dans le cadre de son programme d’études au doctorat nécessiterait un permis de travail COOP.
- * Est-ce que l’étudiant devrait avoir une autorisation de travail ou de stage s’il allait dans l’établissement universitaire B pour mener des activités de recherche qui ne sont pas directement liées à son projet d’études?

- * Si l’étudiant n'était pas inscrit dans l’établissement A, mais plutôt dans un établissement d'enseignement C à l’étranger et qu’il venait faire aussi des essais dans le même établissement universitaire B au Canada, est-il juste de dire qu’il s’agirait alors d’un stage parce que les activités de recherche qu’il viendrait mener ne feraient alors pas partie intégrante d’un programme d’études offert au Canada pourlequel il aurait un permis d’études?

Answer: When the work experience is entered into the Express Entry Profile Builder, the two separate periods of work experience will not be considered as continuous work experience. While the applicant is continuously employed, maternity leave would be considered an interruption in their continuous work experience. Answer: Requirements differ between Express Entry programs regarding the eligibility of work experience gained as a student:
Canadian Experience Class (CEC):
- * Work experience gained while a candidate was a full-time student (even if the candidate was on a co-op work term) doesn't count toward the minimum requirements for the CEC program.
Federal Skilled Worker Program (FSWP):
- * Experience gained while studying may count towards a candidate's minimum requirements if the work:
o * was paid by wages or commissions
o * was continuous (no gaps in employment), and
o * meets all the other reguirements of the Program
For work hours, 780 hours in 8 months at 20 hours per week is not enough to meet the 1,560-hour minimum required for full-time equivalency. The candidate can meet the 1,560-hour requirement in a few different ways:
- * full time at 1 job: up to 30 hours/week for 12 months = 1 year full time (1,560 hours)
- * equal amount in part-time work: for example, 15 hours/week for 24 months = 1 year full time (1,560 hours) o * The candidate can work as many part-time jobs as are needed to meet this requirement.
- * full time at more than 1 job: 30 hours/week for 12 months at more than 1 job = 1 year full time (1,560 hours)

A candidate may be assigned Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) for having ‘two or more post-secondary program credentials' as per section 11(1)(a)(vi) of the Ministerial Instructions respecting the Express Entry system, if the education credentials represent separate certificates, diplomas, or degrees. If one credential is used as a component of the second credential, then those are not considered two separate credentials even though two separate certificates, diplomas, or degrees were awarded. To obtain points for having two or more post-secondary credentials, at least one of them must be issued at the completion of a post-secondary program of three years or more.
